note: Fuel consumption and coolant thermal-management constants (issue #111). The only home for a ground-vehicle fuel or coolant constant. Every value carries a source id that resolves in the sources array, or a named derivation. The generator tools/gen_fuel_data.py projects this file to addons/vehicles/functions/fnc_getFuelData.sqf. The validator tools/validation/validate_fuel_data.py gates it. The runtime kernel never invents a value: a class or surface the file does not hold resolves no constant and the model refuses.

sources.title: Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals

sources.title: Fundamentals of Vehicle Dynamics

sources.title: Surface Vehicle Standard: Engine Power Test Code - Spark Ignition and Compression Ignition - Net Power Rating

sources.title: AEE issue #111 research brief: vehicle fuel consumption and thermal management
sources.note: The research brief that states the coolant thresholds, the terrain multipliers and the military consumption anchors. A compilation: the values it states are held at grade claimed, and each is corroborated against the reference works where they overlap.

sources.title: Progress in Reducing Aerodynamic Drag for Higher Efficiency of Heavy Duty Trucks (Class 7-8)

engine_classes.locator: Brake-specific fuel consumption maps for spark-ignition engines; the best point is near 225 g/kWh at the 60-80 percent torque island.
engine_classes.basis: best-point BSFC for a naturally-aspirated petrol engine

engine_classes.locator: Brake-specific fuel consumption for boosted spark-ignition engines; the rich-mixture protection and the boost penalty place the best point at 230-250 g/kWh.
engine_classes.basis: best-point BSFC for a turbocharged petrol engine, the low end of the 230-250 g/kWh band

engine_classes.locator: Brake-specific fuel consumption for compression-ignition engines; the best point is 200-215 g/kWh and the sweet spot is 206 g/kWh at about 40.6 percent thermal efficiency.
engine_classes.basis: best-point BSFC for a diesel engine

fuels.locator: Fuel properties; petrol density near 740 g/L and lower heating value near 43.9 MJ/kg.

fuels.basis: published diesel density and lower heating value
